verdict.rationale: Galileo documents its own alert rules: you configure a metric, an aggregation function, a threshold and a time window, and it alerts you when unexpected things happen, such as cost spikes or rising hallucinations. That is a native rule-on-event trigger, but the only documented action is an alert; nothing shows rules running arbitrary downstream actions. missing for 10: actions other than alert notifications (e.g., blocking, rerouting, or running workflows), documented delivery channels or webhook targets, event types beyond metric thresholds, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Galileo enables you to get alerted whenever unexpected things happen.
Each alert configuration includes: a metric e.g. Cost, Correctness, Context Adherence; an aggregation function...; a threshold e.g. < 0.5; a time window e.g. 1 hour
Your cost is higher than expected, Your model is hallucinating more than you want
